name: creation
summary: Tensor construction, and the seeding of the default generator.
extended:
Thirty entry points: conversion (`tensor`, `as_tensor`, `from_numpy`), filled and `*_like` constructors, the range builders `arange` / `linspace`, the sampling family, the generator controls (`seed`, `get_rng_state` / `set_rng_state`, `initial_seed`, `randperm`) and DLPack exchange.

Every constructor takes `device=`, and passing it is what keeps a pipeline on one device: a helper built without it lands on the CPU and forces a round trip the moment it meets Metal data.

CPU and Metal share one default generator but consume it differently per draw — a CPU `rand(4)` advances its counter by 4, a Metal `rand(4)` by one block — so the same seed does not reproduce the same stream across devices; comparing them means comparing deterministic ops, replaying state with `get_rng_state()` / `set_rng_state()`, or `eval()` for anything stochastic.

methods.name: seed
methods.summary: Reseed the stream from the OS entropy source and return the new key.

returns.description:
The key, in $[0, 2^{63})$; `manual_seed` with it
replays the stream from here.

methods.name: counter
methods.summary: How many Philox blocks the stream has drawn since it was seeded — the engine's own property, named here so it stays this class's member as it was when `lucid.Generator` was the engine class.

members.summary: A Philox-4×32 random stream of its own.
members.extended:
Pass one as `generator=` to a random op to draw from it instead of the
default stream that `lucid.manual_seed` controls; draws through it
leave the default stream where it was.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description:
The key, any integer in $[-2^{63}, 2^{64})$ — a negative one
is read modulo $2^{64}$, as the reference reads it.  When a
device specifier is given as the single positional argument
(`Generator("cpu")`), it is read as `device` and the key
defaults to `0`.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: The device recorded on `device`.  Defaults to `device("cpu")`.

raises.description: If `seed` is not an integer or device specifier.

If `seed` is out of the 64-bit range or `device` names no
supported device.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> g = lucid.Generator().manual_seed(7)
>>> g.initial_seed()
7
>>> a = lucid.rand(3, generator=g)
>>> state = g.get_state()
>>> b = lucid.rand(3, generator=g)
>>> c = lucid.rand(3, generator=g.set_state(state))
>>> bool((b == c).all())
True
notes:
The constructor accepts both `Generator(seed)` and the reference's
`Generator(device=...)` / `Generator("cpu")`.  `seed` reseeds
from entropy, as the reference's does; `initial_seed` reads the
key.

members.summary: Return a tensor of samples drawn from a parametric normal distribution.
members.extended:
Each element is drawn independently from $\mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$:

$$
X_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu,\, \sigma^2), \quad
f_X(x) = \frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\,
         \exp\!\left(-\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)
$$

with mean $\mathbb{E}[X_i] = \mu$ and standard deviation
$\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}[X_i]} = \sigma$.

parameters.name: mean
parameters.description:
Mean $\mu$ of the distribution.  Default: `0.0`.  A tensor
selects the reference's tensor overloads (see Notes).

parameters.name: std
parameters.description: Standard deviation $\sigma \ge 0$.  Default: `1.0`.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description:
Shape of the output tensor.  Required with a float `mean` and
`std` (keyword, or third positional); none with a tensor.

parameters.name: dtype
parameters.description: Floating-point data type.  Defaults to the global default.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Target device — `"cpu"` or `"metal"`.

parameters.name: requires_grad
parameters.description: Enable autograd tracking.  Default: `False`.

parameters.name: generator
parameters.description: Explicit generator.  Defaults to the global default.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> _ = lucid.manual_seed(0)
>>> x = lucid.normal(mean=5.0, std=2.0, size=(1000,))
>>> abs(float(x.mean()) - 5.0) < 0.2
True
>>> abs(float(x.std()) - 2.0) < 0.2
True
>>> lucid.normal(lucid.zeros(2, 3), lucid.ones(3)).shape  # per-element
(2, 3)
>>> lucid.normal(0.0, 1.0, (4,)).shape  # shape by position
(4,)
He-normal initialisation for a Conv2d kernel:
>>> fan_in = 3 * 3 * 64          # kernel_h × kernel_w × C_in
>>> w = lucid.normal(0.0, (2.0 / fan_in) ** 0.5, size=(128, 64, 3, 3))
notes:
This is a convenience wrapper around `randn` with an affine shift:



$$
X = \mu + \sigma \cdot Z, \quad Z \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)
$$

The output is therefore equivalent to
`mean + std * lucid.randn(*size, ...)`.

With a tensor `mean` or `std` it draws one sample per element of
their broadcast shape, in the dtype they promote to, with no gradient to
either; only `generator=` is taken besides.

**Weight initialisation** recipes commonly parameterise the normal
distribution directly:

* **LeCun normal** (LeCun et al., 1998):
  $\sigma = \sqrt{1 / n_\text{in}}$
* **Glorot normal** (Glorot & Bengio, 2010):
  $\sigma = \sqrt{2 / (n_\text{in} + n_\text{out})}$
* **[He normal** (He et al., 2015)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.01852):
  $\sigma = \sqrt{2 / n_\text{in}}$

members.summary: Return a tensor of samples drawn from the continuous uniform distribution.
members.extended:
Each element is drawn independently from $U[0, 1)$, the uniform
distribution on the half-open unit interval:

$$
X_i \sim U[0, 1), \quad
f_X(x) = \begin{cases} 1 & 0 \le x < 1 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$

The distribution has mean $\mathbb{E}[X] = \tfrac{1}{2}$ and variance
$\operatorname{Var}[X] = \tfrac{1}{12}$.

parameters.name: *size
parameters.description:
Shape of the output tensor.  Accepts varargs `rand(2, 3)`, a
single tuple `rand((2, 3))` or the keyword `rand(size=(2, 3))`.

parameters.name: dtype
parameters.description:
Floating-point data type.  Defaults to the global default
(`lucid.float32`).  Integer dtypes are not supported.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Target device — `"cpu"` or `"metal"`.

parameters.name: requires_grad
parameters.description:
If `True`, downstream operations are tracked by autograd.
Default: `False`.

parameters.name: generator
parameters.description:
Explicit generator to use.  When `None` (default), the global
default generator is used.

returns.description: Tensor of shape `size` with values in $[0, 1)$.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> _ = lucid.manual_seed(0)
>>> x = lucid.rand(3, 4)
>>> x.shape
(3, 4)
>>> float(x.min()) >= 0.0 and float(x.max()) < 1.0
True
Monte-Carlo estimate of $\pi$:
>>> _ = lucid.manual_seed(0)
>>> n = 1_000_000
>>> pts = lucid.rand(n, 2)
>>> inside = ((pts ** 2).sum(dim=-1) < 1.0).float().mean()
>>> abs(float(inside) * 4 - 3.1416) < 0.01
True

members.name: randint
members.signature: randint(low: int, high: int, size: list[int] | tuple[int, ...], dtype: DTypeLike = None, device: DeviceLike = None, requires_grad: bool = False, generator: _C_engine.Generator | None = None)
members.summary: Return a tensor of samples drawn from the discrete uniform distribution.
members.extended:
Each element is drawn independently and uniformly from the integer set
$\{l, l+1, \ldots, h-1\}$, i.e. the discrete uniform distribution:

$$
X_i \sim \mathcal{U}\{l,\, h-1\}, \quad
P(X_i = k) = \frac{1}{h - l}
\quad \forall\; k \in \{l, \ldots, h-1\}
$$

The distribution has mean $\mathbb{E}[X] = \tfrac{l + h - 1}{2}$ and
variance $\operatorname{Var}[X] = \tfrac{(h-l)^2 - 1}{12}$.

parameters.name: low
parameters.description:
Lower bound of the interval (inclusive).  Leave it out for the
reference's two-argument spelling `randint(high, size)`, which
draws from `[0, high)`.

parameters.name: high
parameters.description:
Upper bound of the interval (exclusive).  Must satisfy
`high > low`.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description:
Shape of the output tensor.  Unlike `rand` / `randn`, `size`
is a single required keyword-positional argument, not varargs.

parameters.name: dtype
parameters.description: Integer data type.  Defaults to `lucid.int64`.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Target device — `"cpu"` or `"metal"`.

parameters.name: requires_grad
parameters.description:
Enable autograd tracking.  Default: `False`.  Gradients through
integer tensors are always zero; this flag is accepted for
compatibility with downstream wrappers.

parameters.name: generator
parameters.description: Explicit generator.  Defaults to the global default generator.

returns.description: Integer tensor of shape `size` with values in $[l, h)$.

raises.description:
`high <= low`, or `dtype` cannot hold `low` or `high - 1`
(`int8` past 127): such a draw used to wrap round.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> _ = lucid.manual_seed(0)
>>> x = lucid.randint(0, 10, (5,))
>>> x.shape, x.dtype
((5,), lucid.int64)
>>> bool(((x >= 0) & (x < 10)).all())
True
>>> lucid.randint(10, (5,)).shape  # high only: values in [0, 10)
(5,)
>>> idx = lucid.randint(0, 1024, (64,))  # sample 64 indices
>>> mask = lucid.randint(0, 2, (3, 4))  # values in {0, 1}
notes:
The engine generates the integers via
$X_i = l + \lfloor U_i \cdot (h - l) \rfloor$ for $U_i \sim U[0, 1)$,
giving an exact discrete uniform distribution with no
acceptance–rejection overhead.  Common uses include sampling mini-batch
indices, generating random class labels, and stochastic depth masks.

members.name: randn
members.signature: randn(size: int | tuple[int, ...] = (), dtype: DTypeLike = None, device: DeviceLike = None, requires_grad: bool = False, generator: _C_engine.Generator | None = None)
members.summary: Return a tensor of samples drawn from the standard normal distribution.
members.extended:
Each element is drawn independently from $\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$, the
standard Gaussian with zero mean and unit variance:

$$
X_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1), \quad
f_X(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\, e^{-x^2 / 2}
$$

The distribution has mean $\mathbb{E}[X] = 0$, variance
$\operatorname{Var}[X] = 1$, and all odd central moments zero.

parameters.name: *size
parameters.description:
Shape of the output tensor: varargs `randn(2, 3)`, a single tuple
`randn((2, 3))` or the keyword `randn(size=(2, 3))`.

parameters.name: dtype
parameters.description: Floating-point data type.  Defaults to the global default.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Target device — `"cpu"` or `"metal"`.

parameters.name: requires_grad
parameters.description: Enable autograd tracking.  Default: `False`.

parameters.name: generator
parameters.description: Explicit generator.  Defaults to the global default generator.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> _ = lucid.manual_seed(0)
>>> x = lucid.randn(1000)
>>> abs(float(x.mean())) < 0.1       # ≈ 0
True
>>> abs(float(x.std()) - 1.0) < 0.1  # ≈ 1
True
Kaiming initialisation for a linear layer:
>>> fan_in = 256
>>> w = lucid.randn(fan_in, 512) * (2.0 / fan_in) ** 0.5
notes:
The engine uses the **Box–Muller transform** to convert pairs of
uniform samples $(u_1, u_2) \sim U(0,1)^2$ into standard normals:



$$
z_1 = \sqrt{-2\ln u_1}\,\cos(2\pi u_2), \quad
z_2 = \sqrt{-2\ln u_1}\,\sin(2\pi u_2)
$$

This is exact (not approximate) and is highly efficient on SIMD
hardware because the two outputs $z_1, z_2$ can be produced
simultaneously from one pair of uniform draws.

**Xavier / Glorot initialisation** (Glorot & Bengio, 2010) uses
$\mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$ with



$$
\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{2}{n_\text{in} + n_\text{out}}}
$$

which can be obtained as `randn(fan_in, fan_out) * sigma`.

**[He / Kaiming initialisation** (He et al., 2015)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.01852) for ReLU networks
uses $\sigma = \sqrt{2 / n_\text{in}}$.
